manifest.title: Relaxing Global Classifier Robustness on Semimetric Spaces

inputs.abstract:
We formalize the mathematical statements of Andrei Aleksandrov and Kim
Völlinger's *Relaxing Global Classifier Robustness on Semimetric Spaces*.
A classifier is (μ,ε)-robust when every input lies within μ of a same-label
point whose closed ε-ball has a constant label.

The concept package includes the covering characterization, the general and
finite-order existence criteria, the precision obstruction Δδμ+Δ, the
noncompositional counterexamples, and the transfer theorem for closed
overlapping decompositions. It also specifies the canonical single-NaN binary
floating-point model, its absolute and squared embedded distances, and the sum
and synchronized maximum constructions on vectors and padded lists.

The public results follow the paper’s structure: five theorems, three
corollaries, Proposition 1’s constructions, and the two counterexamples of
Lemma 1. Equivalences are presented once; their directional arguments and other
supporting facts are separate proof lemmas. All 16 public results are proved in
Lean, reusing intermediate covering, existence, precision and construction
results. The complete package passes LAX validation and kernel replay.

import Lax544225.Semimetric
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Lattice

/-!
---
title: Closed balls and neighborhoods
type: definition
---
The closed ball B(x,r) consists of inputs at distance at most r from x. The r-neighborhood of a set is the union of balls centered in that set (Definition 7, p. 5).

# Formalization notes

Closed inequalities are essential: an input at distance exactly ε must have the same label. Ball membership uses d(y,x), matching the paper.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.Balls

open scoped NNReal

open Semimetric
/-- The closed ball centered at x with radius r. -/
def ball {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (x : S) (r : ℝ≥0) : Set S :=
  {y | d y x ≤ r}

/-- The union of closed r-balls with centers in A. -/
def neighborhood {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (A : Set S) (r : ℝ≥0) : Set S :=
  {y | ∃ x ∈ A, y ∈ ball d x r}

end Lax544225.Balls

concepts.sourceText:
import Lax544225.OrderedSemimetric
import Mathlib.Data.Real.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Int.Cast.Lemmas

/-!
---
title: Canonical binary floats and their embedding
type: definition
---
A binary format has p fractional mantissa bits and an exponent interval. Its canonical finite values are supplemented by signed zeros, signed infinities, and one NaN. The real embedding φ separates the special values as in Proposition 1 (p. 8).

# Formalization notes

This is the paper’s single-NaN abstraction, matching the supplied Flocq BinarySingleNaN examples, not the full set of IEEE NaN payloads. A finite mantissa is stored as the integer k with m=k·2^(−p); normality means k≥2^p. The independent order puts −∞ first, then negative finite values, −0, +0, positive finite values, +∞, and NaN. It is not defined by φ. The two distances are the absolute and squared differences of φ.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.BinaryFloats

open scoped NNReal

/-- The precision and nonempty exponent interval of a binary format. -/
structure Format where
  /-- Number of fractional bits in the significand. -/
  precision : ℕ
  /-- Least allowed exponent. -/
  minExponent : ℤ
  /-- Greatest allowed exponent. -/
  maxExponent : ℤ
  /-- The exponent interval is nonempty. -/
  exponent_le : minExponent ≤ maxExponent

/-- Canonical data for a nonzero finite number in a format. -/
structure FiniteValue (F : Format) where
  /-- Sign bit: 0 is positive and 1 is negative. -/
  sign : Fin 2
  /-- The exponent of the value. -/
  exponent : ℤ
  /-- The integer significand before scaling by 2^(−p). -/
  mantissa : ℕ
  /-- The exponent is allowed by the format. -/
  exponent_mem : F.minExponent ≤ exponent ∧ exponent ≤ F.maxExponent
  /-- The significand is nonzero and less than 2^(p+1). -/
  mantissa_mem : 0 < mantissa ∧ mantissa < 2 ^ (F.precision + 1)
  /-- A significand below the normal range occurs only at the minimum exponent. -/
  canonical : 2 ^ F.precision ≤ mantissa ∨ exponent = F.minExponent

/-- Canonical finite data and the four signed special values together with one NaN. -/
inductive Value (F : Format)
  /-- A nonzero finite floating-point value. -/
  | finite : FiniteValue F → Value F
  /-- A signed zero. -/
  | zero : Fin 2 → Value F
  /-- A signed infinity. -/
  | infinity : Fin 2 → Value F
  /-- The single, greatest NaN value. -/
  | nan : Value F

/-- The exact ordinary real value of canonical finite data. -/
noncomputable def finiteReal {F : Format} (f : FiniteValue F) : ℝ :=
  (-1 : ℝ) ^ f.sign.val * (2 : ℝ) ^ f.exponent *
    ((f.mantissa : ℝ) * (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(F.precision : ℤ)))

/-- The real embedding including separated signed zeros and bounded special values. -/
noncomputable def phi (F : Format) : Value F → ℝ
  | .finite f => finiteReal f
  | .zero s => if s.val = 0 then 0 else -(2 : ℝ) ^ (F.minExponent - (F.precision : ℤ) - 1)
  | .infinity s => if s.val = 0 then (2 : ℝ) ^ (F.maxExponent + 1)
    else -(2 : ℝ) ^ (F.maxExponent + 1)
  | .nan => (2 : ℝ) ^ (F.maxExponent + 1) + 1

/-- The position of each sign and special-value category in the total order. -/
def category {F : Format} : Value F → ℕ
  | .finite f => if f.sign.val = 0 then 4 else 1
  | .zero s => if s.val = 0 then 3 else 2
  | .infinity s => if s.val = 0 then 5 else 0
  | .nan => 6

/-- The ordinary finite value used to order members within a finite category. -/
noncomputable def withinCategory {F : Format} : Value F → ℝ
  | .finite f => finiteReal f
  | _ => 0

/-- IEEE category order with one positive NaN and exact comparison of finite values. -/
def ieeeLe (F : Format) (x y : Value F) : Prop :=
  category x < category y ∨
    (category x = category y ∧ withinCategory x ≤ withinCategory y)

/-- Absolute embedded distance d₁. -/
noncomputable def absDistance (F : Format) (x y : Value F) : ℝ≥0 :=
  Real.toNNReal (|phi F x - phi F y|)

/-- Squared embedded distance d₂. -/
noncomputable def squareDistance (F : Format) (x y : Value F) : ℝ≥0 :=
  Real.toNNReal ((phi F x - phi F y) ^ 2)

end Lax544225.BinaryFloats

import Lax544225.Covering
import Mathlib.Order.Interval.Set.Basic

/-!
---
title: Successors and cut boundaries
type: definition
---
In a total order, y is the immediate successor of x when x<y and no point lies strictly between them. The boundary of a subset consists of its points adjacent to a point outside it. The complement boundary is the boundary of the complement (Section 5.2, p. 10).

# Formalization notes

The boundary covering condition restricts the μ-ball to the side containing its center, and uses ε-balls centered in the boundary on the opposite side. This preserves the two distinct boundaries in Theorem 3.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.Boundary

open scoped NNReal

open Semimetric Balls
/-- Consecutive points in a linear order. -/
def Successor {S : Type u} [LinearOrder S] (x y : S) : Prop :=
  x < y ∧ ¬ ∃ z, x < z ∧ z < y

/-- Points of A adjacent to its complement in the ambient order. -/
def boundary {S : Type u} [LinearOrder S] (A : Set S) : Set S :=
  {x | x ∈ A ∧ ∃ y ∈ Aᶜ, Successor x y ∨ Successor y x}

/-- Every nontrivial cut has a side-restricted μ-ball covered by the opposite boundary. -/
def EveryCutBoundaryCovered {S : Type u} [LinearOrder S] (d : Distance S)
    (μ ε : ℝ≥0) : Prop :=
  ∀ A : Set S, A.Nonempty → Aᶜ.Nonempty →
    ∃ x, (x ∈ A ∧ ball d x μ ∩ A ⊆ neighborhood d (boundary Aᶜ) ε) ∨
      (x ∈ Aᶜ ∧ ball d x μ ∩ Aᶜ ⊆ neighborhood d (boundary A) ε)

end Lax544225.Boundary

import Lax544225.Boundary
import Lax544225.OrderedSemimetric

/-!
---
title: Theorem 3 — Boundary covering characterization
type: theorem
---
In a finite totally ordered semimetric space, covering every proper cut is equivalent to covering its within-side μ-ball from the opposite boundary (Theorem 3, p. 10).

# Formalization notes

Both directions are stated together as in the paper. Their separate arguments
remain supporting lemmas in the proof package.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.BoundaryCoveringCharacterization

open scoped NNReal
open Semimetric OrderedSemimetric Covering Boundary

/-- In a finite totally ordered semimetric space, covering every proper cut is equivalent to covering its within-side μ-ball from the opposite boundary (Theorem 3, p. 10). -/

    (hd : IsOrdered d (· ≤ ·)) (μ ε : ℝ≥0) (hε : 0 < ε) :
    EveryCutCovered d μ ε ↔ EveryCutBoundaryCovered d μ ε

end Lax544225.BoundaryCoveringCharacterization

title: Classifiers
type: definition
---
A classifier on S with n classes is a total surjective function from S to the n labels (Definition 1, p. 3).

Fin n labels the classes from 0 to n−1; adding 1 recovers the paper’s labels 1 to n. Surjectivity is retained. Existence of a classifier on a nonempty carrier implies n > 0.

  /-- Every class has a representative. -/
  surjective : Function.Surjective label

concepts.title: Local and relaxed classifier robustness
concepts.description: Local ε-robustness means that the ε-ball of an input has its label. Global ε-robustness requires this at every input. Relaxed (μ,ε)-robustness requires every input to have a same-label, locally ε-robust point within distance μ (Definitions 3–4, pp. 3–4).

import Lax544225.Classifier
import Lax544225.Balls

/-!
---
title: Local and relaxed classifier robustness
type: definition
---
Local ε-robustness means that the ε-ball of an input has its label. Global ε-robustness requires this at every input. Relaxed (μ,ε)-robustness requires every input to have a same-label, locally ε-robust point within distance μ (Definitions 3–4, pp. 3–4).

# Formalization notes

Radii are nonnegative reals. The predicates also make sense at ε=0; the paper’s results below explicitly require ε>0. The same-label requirement is present even when μ>ε.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.ClassifierRobustness

open scoped NNReal

open Classifier Semimetric
/-- Local robustness of the classifier at x. -/
def LocallyRobust {S : Type u} {n : ℕ} (d : Distance S)
    (c : Classifier S n) (ε : ℝ≥0) (x : S) : Prop :=
  ∀ y, d y x ≤ ε → c.label y = c.label x

/-- Local robustness at every input. -/
def GloballyRobust {S : Type u} {n : ℕ} (d : Distance S)
    (c : Classifier S n) (ε : ℝ≥0) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, LocallyRobust d c ε x

/-- Coverage of each input by a same-label locally robust input. -/
def RelaxedRobust {S : Type u} {n : ℕ} (d : Distance S)
    (c : Classifier S n) (μ ε : ℝ≥0) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, ∃ x', d x x' ≤ μ ∧ c.label x = c.label x' ∧ LocallyRobust d c ε x'

end Lax544225.ClassifierRobustness

concepts.title: Covering obstructions
concepts.description: The partition covering condition says that the μ-ball of a point in a part is not covered by ε-balls centered outside that part. The global cut obstruction requires every nonempty proper subset to have a point on one side whose μ-ball is covered from the other side (Theorems 1–2, pp. 6, 9).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown: A proper nonempty subset has both itself and its complement nonempty. Neither the empty cut nor the whole carrier is tested. These predicates describe the covering conditions independently of robustness.

import Lax544225.Balls

/-!
---
title: Covering obstructions
type: definition
---
The partition covering condition says that the μ-ball of a point in a part is not covered by ε-balls centered outside that part. The global cut obstruction requires every nonempty proper subset to have a point on one side whose μ-ball is covered from the other side (Theorems 1–2, pp. 6, 9).

# Formalization notes

A proper nonempty subset has both itself and its complement nonempty. Neither the empty cut nor the whole carrier is tested. These predicates describe the covering conditions independently of robustness.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.Covering

open scoped NNReal

open Semimetric Balls
/-- No μ-ball centered in a part is covered by ε-balls from its complement. -/
def Uncovered {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (P : Set (Set S)) (μ ε : ℝ≥0) : Prop :=
  ∀ A ∈ P, ∀ x ∈ A, ¬ ball d x μ ⊆ neighborhood d Aᶜ ε

/-- Every nontrivial cut admits an opposite-side covering obstruction. -/
def EveryCutCovered {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (μ ε : ℝ≥0) : Prop :=
  ∀ A : Set S, A.Nonempty → Aᶜ.Nonempty →
    ∃ x, (x ∈ A ∧ ball d x μ ⊆ neighborhood d Aᶜ ε) ∨
      (x ∈ Aᶜ ∧ ball d x μ ⊆ neighborhood d A ε)

end Lax544225.Covering

concepts.title: Closed overlapping decompositions
concepts.description: A (μ,ε)-decomposition is a finite family of nonempty subsets whose members contain every μ-ball centered in them and which connect every pair of inputs through a finite chain of overlapping members (Definition 11, p. 13).

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown: The definition depends only on μ; ε appears in the applications. ReflTransGen encodes a finite chain, including a chain consisting of a single member. Membership of each endpoint member and each link is explicit. Finiteness concerns the family, not the sizes of its members.

import Lax544225.Balls
import Mathlib.Logic.Relation
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Finite.Basic

/-!
---
title: Closed overlapping decompositions
type: definition
---
A (μ,ε)-decomposition is a finite family of nonempty subsets whose members contain every μ-ball centered in them and which connect every pair of inputs through a finite chain of overlapping members (Definition 11, p. 13).

# Formalization notes

The definition depends only on μ; ε appears in the applications. ReflTransGen encodes a finite chain, including a chain consisting of a single member. Membership of each endpoint member and each link is explicit. Finiteness concerns the family, not the sizes of its members.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.Decomposition

open scoped NNReal

open Semimetric Balls
/-- A finite family of nonempty μ-closed pieces connected by overlaps. -/
def IsDecomposition {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (D : Set (Set S)) (μ : ℝ≥0) : Prop :=
  D.Finite ∧ (∀ A ∈ D, A.Nonempty) ∧
    (∀ A ∈ D, ∀ x ∈ A, ball d x μ ⊆ A) ∧
    (∀ x y, ∃ A ∈ D, ∃ B ∈ D, x ∈ A ∧ y ∈ B ∧
      Relation.ReflTransGen (fun C E => C ∈ D ∧ E ∈ D ∧ (C ∩ E).Nonempty) A B)

end Lax544225.Decomposition

concepts.description: If a semimetric space has a (μ,ε)-decomposition and each induced subspace admits only trivial (μ,ε)-robust partitions, then the whole space admits only trivial (μ,ε)-robust partitions (Theorem 5, pp. 13–14).

import Lax544225.PartitionRobustness

/-!

title: Theorem 5 — Decomposition transfers triviality
type: theorem
---
If a semimetric space has a (μ,ε)-decomposition and each induced subspace admits only trivial (μ,ε)-robust partitions, then the whole space admits only trivial (μ,ε)-robust partitions (Theorem 5, pp. 13–14).

-/

universe u

open scoped NNReal

open Semimetric Decomposition PartitionRobustness

/-- If a semimetric space has a (μ,ε)-decomposition and each induced subspace admits only trivial (μ,ε)-robust partitions, then the whole space admits only trivial (μ,ε)-robust partitions (Theorem 5, pp. 13–14). -/

    (hlocal : ∀ A ∈ D, OnlyTrivial (restrict d A) μ ε) : OnlyTrivial d μ ε

end Lax544225.DecompositionObstruction

import Lax544225.ProductSpaces
import Mathlib.Data.List.GetD

/-!
---
title: Padded list distances
type: definition
---
For finite lists, distances compare coordinates through the longer length, padding missing entries by a chosen point. A distance penalty of 1 is added for different lengths. Orders compare only equal-length lists, using the product or synchronized relation (Proposition 1.5, p. 8).

# Formalization notes

The floating-point instance chooses NaN as padding. Without the length penalty, appending NaN would give distance zero between different lists. The list maximum construction uses an additive base distance just as the fixed-length construction does.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.ListSpaces

open scoped NNReal

open Semimetric
open scoped BigOperators
/-- Equal-length lists ordered coordinatewise; other lengths are incomparable. -/
def listLe {S : Type u} (le : S → S → Prop) (pad : S) (f g : List S) : Prop :=
  f.length = g.length ∧ ∀ i < f.length, le (f.getD i pad) (g.getD i pad)

/-- Equal-length coordinatewise order with equal base distances across coordinates. -/
def synchronizedListLe {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (le : S → S → Prop)
    (pad : S) (f g : List S) : Prop :=
  listLe le pad f g ∧ ∀ i < f.length, ∀ j < f.length,
    d (f.getD i pad) (g.getD i pad) = d (f.getD j pad) (g.getD j pad)

/-- A positive penalty that distinguishes different list lengths. -/
def lengthPenalty {S : Type u} (f g : List S) : ℝ≥0 :=
  if f.length = g.length then 0 else 1

/-- Sum of padded coordinate distances, plus the length penalty. -/
noncomputable def sumDistance {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (pad : S) : Distance (List S) :=
  fun f g => lengthPenalty f g +
    ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (max f.length g.length), d (f.getD i pad) (g.getD i pad)

/-- Maximum padded coordinate distance, plus the length penalty. -/
noncomputable def maxDistance {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (pad : S) : Distance (List S) :=
  fun f g => lengthPenalty f g +
    (Finset.range (max f.length g.length)).sup (fun i => d (f.getD i pad) (g.getD i pad))

end Lax544225.ListSpaces

import Lax544225.Semimetric
import Mathlib.Order.Defs.PartialOrder

/-!
---
title: Ordered semimetric spaces
type: definition
---
An ordered semimetric space has a partial order with d(a,b)+d(b,c)≤d(a,c) whenever a≤b≤c (Definition 9, p. 7). An additive ordered distance satisfies equality on these chains.

# Formalization notes

The order is an explicit non-strict relation. IsPartialOrder provides reflexivity, transitivity, and antisymmetry. The reverse triangle inequality is imposed only on ordered chains. Additivity is an additional property needed for synchronized maximum distances.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.OrderedSemimetric

open Semimetric
/-- The semimetric, partial-order, and ordered-chain distance laws. -/
def IsOrdered {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (le : S → S → Prop) : Prop :=
  IsSemimetric d ∧ IsPartialOrder S le ∧
    (∀ a b c, le a b → le b c → d a b + d b c ≤ d a c)

/-- Exact additivity of distance along the given ordered chains. -/
def Additive {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (le : S → S → Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ a b c, le a b → le b c → d a c = d a b + d b c

end Lax544225.OrderedSemimetric

import Lax544225.Partitions
import Lax544225.Balls

/-!
---
title: Robust and separated partitions
type: definition
---
A partition is (μ,ε)-robust when each input x has a nearby center x′ whose ε-ball and x lie in one part (Definition 8, p. 5). A partition is ε-separated when points in distinct parts are more than ε apart.

# Formalization notes

Partition validity is a separate hypothesis, not built into the robustness predicate. Triviality of every robust partition quantifies over finite valid partitions. Separation uses a strict inequality because balls are closed.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.PartitionRobustness

open scoped NNReal

open Semimetric Partitions Balls
/-- Coverage by monochromatic balls whose centers are μ-close to the input. -/
def Robust {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (P : Set (Set S)) (μ ε : ℝ≥0) : Prop :=
  ∀ x, ∃ x', x' ∈ ball d x μ ∧ ∃ A ∈ P, x ∈ A ∧ ball d x' ε ⊆ A

/-- Distinct parts are separated by distance strictly greater than ε. -/
def Separated {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (P : Set (Set S)) (ε : ℝ≥0) : Prop :=
  ∀ A ∈ P, ∀ B ∈ P, A ≠ B → ∀ x ∈ A, ∀ y ∈ B, ε < d x y

/-- Every robust finite partition of the carrier has only the whole carrier as a part. -/
def OnlyTrivial {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (μ ε : ℝ≥0) : Prop :=
  ∀ P, IsPartition P → Robust d P μ ε → IsTrivial P

end Lax544225.PartitionRobustness

import Lax544225.Classifier
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Finite.Basic

/-!
---
title: Finite partitions and classifier fibers
type: definition
---
A partition is a finite collection of nonempty pairwise disjoint subsets covering S. The trivial partition has the single part S. A classifier induces the collection of its label fibers (Definitions 5–6, p. 5).

# Formalization notes

The family is a set of sets, so enumeration and duplicate parts are absent. Unique membership expresses covering and pairwise disjointness together. Finite families are required even when S is infinite.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.Partitions

open Classifier
/-- A finite partition into nonempty parts with unique membership for every input. -/
def IsPartition {S : Type u} (P : Set (Set S)) : Prop :=
  P.Finite ∧ (∀ A ∈ P, A.Nonempty) ∧ (∀ x, ∃! A, A ∈ P ∧ x ∈ A)

/-- The partition consisting of the whole carrier as its only part. -/
def IsTrivial {S : Type u} (P : Set (Set S)) : Prop := P = {Set.univ}

/-- The part assigned a particular classifier label. -/
def fiber {S : Type u} {n : ℕ} (c : Classifier S n) (i : Fin n) : Set S :=
  {x | c.label x = i}

/-- The collection of all label fibers. -/
def induced {S : Type u} {n : ℕ} (c : Classifier S n) : Set (Set S) :=
  Set.range (fiber c)

end Lax544225.Partitions

import Lax544225.Semimetric
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card
import Mathlib.Data.NNReal.Defs
import Mathlib.Order.Interval.Set.Basic

/-!
---
title: Precision gap measures
type: definition
---
For a finite linearly ordered semimetric space with at least two points, Δ is the maximum of d(x,y)/(|[x,y]|−1), and δ is the maximum of the reciprocal ratio (Definition 10, pp. 11–12).

# Formalization notes

The formulas are defined for partial orders and used only on finite totally ordered carriers or pieces. The interval uses the ambient order of that carrier or piece. Natural cardinalities are cast into ℝ≥0 before division. Suprema of the finite ratio sets are their maxima. On a singleton the ratio sets are empty and Δ=δ=0, extending the paper’s undefined singleton case so decomposition pieces of size one need no arbitrary parameters. Δ equals the largest adjacent gap only for an additive distance; no such equality is presumed for general semimetrics.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.PrecisionGaps

open scoped NNReal

open Semimetric
/-- The number of consecutive steps between the endpoints of a closed interval. -/
noncomputable def steps {S : Type u} [PartialOrder S] (x y : S) : ℕ :=
  (Set.Icc x y).ncard - 1

/-- The largest average distance per ordered step. -/
noncomputable def deltaUpper {S : Type u} [PartialOrder S] (d : Distance S) : ℝ≥0 :=
  sSup {r | ∃ x y, x < y ∧ r = d x y / (steps x y : ℝ≥0)}

/-- The largest number of ordered steps per unit distance. -/
noncomputable def deltaInverse {S : Type u} [PartialOrder S] (d : Distance S) : ℝ≥0 :=
  sSup {r | ∃ x y, x < y ∧ r = (steps x y : ℝ≥0) / d x y}

/-- The paper’s precision-dependent obstruction threshold Δδμ+Δ. -/
noncomputable def threshold {S : Type u} [PartialOrder S] (d : Distance S)
    (μ : ℝ≥0) : ℝ≥0 := deltaUpper d * deltaInverse d * μ + deltaUpper d

end Lax544225.PrecisionGaps

/-!

title: Sum and synchronized maximum product distances
type: definition

On n-tuples, the sum distance uses the product partial order. The maximum distance uses the synchronized subrelation of that order: every coordinate changes by the same base distance. The maximum construction requires the base distance to be additive on chains (Proposition 1.3–1.4, p. 8).

namespace Lax544225.ProductSpaces

open Semimetric
open scoped BigOperators
/-- Coordinatewise order on finite tuples. -/
def productLe {S : Type u} (le : S → S → Prop) (n : ℕ) (f g : Fin n → S) : Prop :=
  ∀ i, le (f i) (g i)

/-- Coordinatewise order restricted to equal distances in every coordinate. -/
def synchronizedLe {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (le : S → S → Prop) (n : ℕ)
    (f g : Fin n → S) : Prop :=
  productLe le n f g ∧ ∀ i j, d (f i) (g i) = d (f j) (g j)

noncomputable def sumDistance {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (n : ℕ) : Distance (Fin n → S) :=
  fun f g => ∑ i, d (f i) (g i)

/-- Maximum of the base distances between corresponding coordinates. -/
noncomputable def maxDistance {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (n : ℕ) : Distance (Fin n → S) :=
  fun f g => Finset.univ.sup (fun i => d (f i) (g i))

end Lax544225.ProductSpaces

/-!

title: Semimetric spaces
type: definition

A semimetric space is a nonempty set equipped with a symmetric, nonnegative real distance that is zero exactly on equal inputs. No triangle inequality is imposed (Definition 2, p. 3).

# Formalization notes

/-- A nonnegative real-valued distance on a carrier. -/
abbrev Distance (S : Type u) := S → S → ℝ≥0

/-- The defining properties of a semimetric space, including a nonempty carrier. -/
def IsSemimetric {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) : Prop :=
  Nonempty S ∧ (∀ x y, d x y = 0 ↔ x = y) ∧ (∀ x y, d x y = d y x)

/-- The distance inherited by a subset. -/
def restrict {S : Type u} (d : Distance S) (A : Set S) : Distance A :=
  fun x y => d x.val y.val

end Lax544225.Semimetric

import Lax544225.Boundary
import Lax544225.PrecisionGaps
import Lax544225.OrderedSemimetric

/-!
---
title: Theorem 4 — Successor covering at the precision bound
type: theorem
---
In a finite totally ordered semimetric space, ε≥Δδμ+Δ implies B(x,μ)⊆B(y,ε) whenever y is the immediate successor of x (Theorem 4, p. 12).

-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.SuccessorCovering

open scoped NNReal

open Semimetric OrderedSemimetric Balls Boundary PrecisionGaps

/-- In a finite totally ordered semimetric space, ε≥Δδμ+Δ implies B(x,μ)⊆B(y,ε) whenever y is the immediate successor of x (Theorem 4, p. 12). -/
axiom statement {S : Type u} [Finite S] [LinearOrder S] (d : Distance S)
    (hd : IsOrdered d (· ≤ ·)) (μ ε : ℝ≥0) (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hbound : threshold d μ ≤ ε) (x y : S) (hxy : Successor x y) :
    ball d x μ ⊆ ball d y ε

end Lax544225.SuccessorCovering

import Lax544225.PartitionRobustness

/-!
---
title: Lemma 1.2 — Union counterexample
type: lemma
---
Two nonempty proper overlapping subsets can each admit only trivial (1,1)-robust partitions while their union is a four-point space admitting a nontrivial (1,1)-robust partition (Lemma 1.2, p. 13).

# Formalization notes

The paper’s witness is the line {0,1,2,3} with A={0,1,2}, B={1,2,3}, and the two-part partition {{0,1},{2,3}}. The conjunction describes this single counterexample witness.
-/

universe u

namespace Lax544225.UnionCounterexample

open Semimetric Partitions PartitionRobustness

/-- Two nonempty proper overlapping subsets can each admit only trivial (1,1)-robust partitions while their union is a four-point space admitting a nontrivial (1,1)-robust partition (Lemma 1.2, p. 13). -/
axiom statement : ∃ (d : Distance (Fin 4)) (A B : Set (Fin 4)) (P : Set (Set (Fin 4))),
    IsSemimetric d ∧ Aᶜ.Nonempty ∧ Bᶜ.Nonempty ∧ (A ∩ B).Nonempty ∧
    A ∪ B = Set.univ ∧ OnlyTrivial (restrict d A) 1 1 ∧
    OnlyTrivial (restrict d B) 1 1 ∧ IsPartition P ∧ Robust d P 1 1 ∧ ¬ IsTrivial P

end Lax544225.UnionCounterexample

statement : Exists fun d =>
  Exists fun A =>
    Exists fun B =>
      Exists fun P =>
        And (Lax544225.Semimetric.IsSemimetric d)
          (And (Set.instCompl.compl A).Nonempty
            (And (Set.instCompl.compl B).Nonempty
              (And (Set.instInter.inter A B).Nonempty
                (And (Eq (Set.instUnion.union A B) Set.univ)
                  (And (Lax544225.PartitionRobustness.OnlyTrivial (Lax544225.Semimetric.restrict d A) 1 1)
                    (And (Lax544225.PartitionRobustness.OnlyTrivial (Lax544225.Semimetric.restrict d B) 1 1)
                      (And (Lax544225.Partitions.IsPartition P)
                        (And (Lax544225.PartitionRobustness.Robust d P 1 1)
                          (Not (Lax544225.Partitions.IsTrivial P))))))))))

proofs.description:
The four-point line has a robust two-part partition, while its middle pair is
locally trivial and crosses both global parts.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Use ordinary integer distance on {0,1,2,3} and the cut at 2. Centers 0 and 3
witness robustness. In the restricted middle pair, every unit ball contains 1,
so the common-ball lemma forces triviality. The pair is in neither global part.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:
Lemma 1.1 of Aleksandrov and Völlinger, *Relaxing Global Classifier Robustness
on Semimetric Spaces*, supplied FSEN 2027 manuscript, p. 13.

proofs.description:
The overlapping triples of the four-point line are locally trivial, although
their union has a nontrivial robust partition.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Reuse the four-point line and split. Every unit ball in {0,1,2} contains 1,
and every unit ball in {1,2,3} contains 2. Apply the common-ball lemma on each
triple and verify their overlap and union directly.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:
Lemma 1.2 of Aleksandrov and Völlinger, *Relaxing Global Classifier Robustness
on Semimetric Spaces*, supplied FSEN 2027 manuscript, p. 13.

proofs.description: Local triviality propagates through a closed overlap decomposition.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Intersect a robust partition with a μ-closed piece and discard empty traces.
The traces form a robust partition of the induced subspace, hence are trivial.
Each piece is therefore monochromatic. A finite overlap chain propagates its
part to any input, forcing that part to be the whole carrier.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:
Theorem 5 of Aleksandrov and Völlinger, *Relaxing Global Classifier Robustness
on Semimetric Spaces*, supplied FSEN 2027 manuscript, pp. 13–14.

proofs.description: Precision bounds on totally ordered decomposition pieces imply global triviality.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Give each piece its inherited linear order, preserving the interval steps in
its precision measures. Apply the total-order precision obstruction on each
piece, then use the closed overlap decomposition theorem.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:
Corollary 3 of Aleksandrov and Völlinger, *Relaxing Global Classifier Robustness
on Semimetric Spaces*, supplied FSEN 2027 manuscript, p. 14.

proofs.description: Absolute embedded distance forms an ordered semimetric.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Injectivity of φ gives distance-zero separation, and absolute differences are
symmetric. Reuse the proved IEEE linear order and scalar chain additivity,
whose equality implies the required antitriangle inequality.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: Proposition 1.1 of the source paper.

proofs.description: Squared embedded distance forms an ordered semimetric.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Injectivity of φ gives distance-zero separation; reversing a difference leaves
its square unchanged. Along an increasing embedded chain, expanding the total
square adds twice the nonnegative product of the adjacent increments.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:
Proposition 1.2 of the source paper and the squared-distance construction in
`flocq_ordered_spaces/semimetrics.v` of verinncoq/mueps-robustness-proofs.

proofs.description: Theorem 3: cut covering is equivalent to covering from opposite boundaries.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Combine the two supporting implications. Between a covered within-side point
and an opposite-side center, choose a consecutive boundary crossing. The ordered
antitriangle law bounds distance to that boundary. To recover whole-ball
coverage, opposite-side points cover themselves with their own ε-balls.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:

on Semimetric Spaces*, supplied FSEN 2027 manuscript, p. 10.

proofs.description: Corollary 1: only-trivial robustness is equivalent to opposite-boundary covering.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Combine the two supporting compositions of Theorem 2 with Theorem 3. The
general existence criterion converts triviality to cut covering, and the
boundary characterization converts cut covering to boundary covering.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:
Corollary 1 of Aleksandrov and Völlinger, *Relaxing Global Classifier Robustness
on Semimetric Spaces*, supplied FSEN 2027 manuscript, pp. 10–11.

proofs.description: Theorem 1: robustness is equivalent to failure of opposite-part coverage.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Combine the two supporting implications. A robust center avoids the
ε-neighborhood of the complement of its part. Conversely, an uncovered μ-ball
supplies a center whose ε-ball stays within the selected part.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:
Theorem 1 of Aleksandrov and Völlinger, *Relaxing Global Classifier Robustness
on Semimetric Spaces*, supplied FSEN 2027 manuscript, p. 6.

proofs.description: Theorem 2: only-trivial robustness is equivalent to coverage of every proper cut.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Combine the two cut arguments, using Theorem 1. An uncovered proper cut and its
complement give a nontrivial robust partition. In the converse direction, a
proper part of a robust partition contradicts coverage of that cut.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:
Theorem 2 of Aleksandrov and Völlinger, *Relaxing Global Classifier Robustness
on Semimetric Spaces*, supplied FSEN 2027 manuscript, p. 9.

proofs.description: Padded synchronized maxima with a length penalty form an ordered semimetric space.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Use the synchronized maximum-product result on the padded coordinate vectors.
The length penalty and tuple separation distinguish lists. Equal-length
comparison transfers the synchronized partial order, including its transitivity,
and the chain distance bound from the corresponding tuple construction.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:
Proposition 1.5 of Aleksandrov and Völlinger's supplied FSEN 2027 manuscript;
the padded length-penalty construction is also present in the cited Rocq reference.

proofs.description: Synchronized finite maxima preserve the ordered semimetric laws.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
A maximum vanishes exactly when every coordinate distance vanishes. Exact
base additivity makes synchronization transitive. On a nonempty synchronized
product the maximum equals any coordinate distance, giving exact chain
additivity; the empty product has distance zero.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:
Proposition 1.4 of Aleksandrov and Völlinger's supplied FSEN 2027 manuscript;
the synchronized construction is also described in the cited Rocq reference.

proofs.description: The precision threshold excludes every nontrivial robust partition.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Each proper cut has a consecutive crossing pair. SuccessorCovering places the
ball at the lower point inside an epsilon-ball centered across the cut. Apply the
previous general cut-covering obstruction.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: Aleksandrov and Völlinger, Corollary 2.

proofs.description: The precision threshold covers a ball from the next ordered point.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Use the finite ratio suprema to bound distance by Delta times interval steps and
steps by delta times distance. A successor adds exactly one interval step. On the
other side of the successor, the ordered antitriangle inequality gives monotonicity.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: Aleksandrov and Völlinger, Theorem 4.

proofs.description: Padded finite sums with a length penalty form an ordered semimetric space.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Transfer the tuple semimetric and partial-order laws through padded coordinate
vectors. A vanishing length penalty forces equal lengths, and tuple separation
then forces list equality. On comparable lists the penalty is zero and all
lengths coincide, so the sum-product antitriangle result applies directly.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: Proposition 1.5 of Aleksandrov and Völlinger's supplied FSEN 2027 manuscript.

proofs.description: Finite sums preserve the ordered semimetric laws.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
Zero sums force coordinate equality; symmetry and the antitriangle law follow
coordinatewise. The empty product is included by the same finite-sum laws.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown: Proposition 1.3 of Aleksandrov and Völlinger's supplied FSEN 2027 manuscript.
